Problem Statement:
Strip problematic private escape sequences

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.

- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

`\x1b` is the ESC character.
The group `([(@-Z\\\\-_]|\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~])` matches:
1. `[@-Z\\\\-_]` which is characters from '@' to 'Z', '\', '-', '_'
2. `\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]` which is CSI (Control Sequence Introducer) `[` followed by parameters.

'0' is 0x30, '?' is 0x3F.
Looking at the regex: `[@-Z\\\\-_]`
'@' is 0x40. 'Z' is 0x5A.
So '0'-'?' (0x30-0x3F) are NOT matched by `[@-Z\\\\-_]`.

If the regex is used for tokenizing and identifying ANSI codes to be processed (and potentially stripped or converted to rich styles), and it DOES NOT match `\x1b0`-`\x1b?`, then those sequences will be treated as plain text.

The `re_ansi` regex is:
```python
re_ansi = re.compile(
    r"""
(?:\\x1b\\](.*?)\\x1b\\\\)|\n(?:\\x1b([(@-Z\\\\-_]|\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))
    """,
    re.VERBOSE,
)
```
Let's analyze `(?:\\x1b([(@-Z\\\\-_]|\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))`.
This part matches `ESC` followed by:
- `[@-Z\\\\-_]` : This is characters with ASCII values from 64 (@) to 90 (Z), and also `\`, `-`, `_`.
- `\\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]` : This is CSI sequences.

Characters '0'-'?' (0x30 to 0x3F, i.e., ASCII 48 to 63) are NOT included in `[@-Z\\\\-_]`.
So `\x1b0`, `\x1b1`, ..., `\x1b?` are NOT matched by `re_ansi`.

When `_ansi_tokenize` runs:
```python
    for match in re_ansi.finditer(ansi_text):
        start, end = match.span(0)
        # ...
        if start > position:
            yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:start])
        # ...
        position = end
    if position < len(ansi_text):
        yield _AnsiToken(ansi_text[position:])
```
If `ansi_text` contains `\x1b7`, and it's not matched by `re_ansi`, it will be included in `ansi_text[position:start]` or `ansi_text[position:]`, which means it's yielded as `plain` text.

The goal is to strip these sequences. To strip them, they must be matched by the regex but not yielded as plain text.

If I add `0-?` to the regex, they will be matched as `sgr`.

```

```

`sgr == "("` is false.
`sgr.endswith("m")` is false.
So it does NOTHING and then `position = end`.
This means it's effectively stripped!
